newsitem.title: USA: 3M posts record first quarter results.
newsitem.headline: 3M posts record first quarter results.

text.p: Minnesota Mining & Manufacturing Co. Tuesday reported record results for the first quarter, driven by growing demand for its diverse products and solid productivity gains.
The company said it earned $410 million, or 99 cents a share, for the three months ended March 31, up 13.3 percent from $362 million, or 87 cents a share, in the year-ago period.
Changes in currency exchange rates reduced earnings by about 5 cents per share, or about 6 percent, it said.
Sales totalled $3.7 billion, an increase of about 11 percent in local currencies and 7.1 percent in U.S. dollars, 3M said.

"Worldwide demand for 3M products continued to be strong during the first quarter. We posted double-digit volume gains in our two business sectors, and in our U.S. and international operations," said Chief Executive L.D. DeSimone.
"A strong flow of innovative products, a sharp focus on customer satisfaction and continued international expansion drove our growth," he added.

The company, based in St. Paul, Minn., makes adhesive tapes, "Post-it" note pads, abrasives, speciality chemicals, computer-based projections, medical devices, reflective materials and major automotive parts.
Worldwide volume sales rose 11 percent, paced by gains in the United States, the Asia Pacific area and Latin America.
Operating income was 18.5 percent of sales, up 1.3 percentage points from the first quarter last year, and an improvement of a full point from 1996 as a whole.

"We're off to a good start for the year and we continue to expect a solid operating performance for 1997 as a whole, despite further strengthening of the U.S. dollar and continued economic softness in much of Western Europe," DeSimone said.
The company's stock added $2.125 to $85.375 in morning trading on the New York Stock Exchange.
